title: Donating Agent Skills to the Agentic AI Foundation
gist: Anthropic donates the Agent Skills open standard — a SKILL.md folder format adopted by 70+ agent platforms with 1M skills published and ~280M installs — to the Linux Foundation's Agentic AI Foundation, following its earlier MCP donation, to make agent interoperability vendor-neutral.

insights.claim: More than 70 agent platforms, including ChatGPT, Cursor, GitHub Copilot and VS Code, have integrated Agent Skills since Anthropic published the standard in December 2025.
insights.speaker: @AnthropicAI
insights.so_what: Rapid cross-vendor adoption suggests Skills is becoming a de facto layer for packaging agent procedural knowledge.

insights.claim: About 1 million skills have been published and nearly 280 million installed, with thousands appearing on GitHub within weeks of the October 2025 launch and community loaders written for Codex, Cursor and OpenCode.
insights.speaker: @AnthropicAI
insights.so_what: Usage scale shows an ecosystem forming around agent skills; a distribution surface for enterprise workflows.

insights.claim: A skill is just a folder containing a SKILL.md file teaching an agent a specific task or domain, plus any scripts or reference material; Anthropic built it in Claude Code to supply the procedural knowledge real business tasks need, which general-knowledge agents lacked.
insights.speaker: @AnthropicAI
insights.so_what: Simplicity of the format is the adoption driver; procedural knowledge packaging is the agent-era analogue of apps.
insights.locator: A skill is a folder containing a SKILL.md file

insights.claim: Anthropic is donating the Agent Skills standard — name, logo, GitHub organization and agentskills.io domain — to the Agentic AI Foundation under the Linux Foundation, which it co-founded with Block and OpenAI and to which it already donated the Model Context Protocol.
insights.speaker: @AnthropicAI
insights.so_what: Anthropic is pursuing a standards-commons strategy (MCP, Skills) to win ecosystem position without owning the protocol; lowers lock-in fears for adopters.

insights.claim: The standard will be maintained by engineers from Anthropic, Google, OpenAI and others acting as individuals, with David Soria Parra and Mahesh Murag as Lead Maintainers, and an initial roadmap of versioned releases, a formal proposal process and security guidance for people who write and install skills.
insights.speaker: @AnthropicAI
insights.so_what: The security-guidance item flags that skill supply-chain risk is a recognized concern as installs scale.
